summary: Round 6 delta is two comment blocks and one assertion. The assertion change is a strengthening in the correct direction and I verified it does real work. MEASURED IN MY OWN TREE, not argued. (1) 26 IS STABLE: nine independent observations -- five --rerun-tasks runs of LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest, three more with the two relative assertions temporarily pinned, and one full ./gradlew test --rerun-tasks -- all green at isEqualTo(26L). Nothing on the path is time- or thread-dependent: MemoryBinStore, a frozen CheckpointWriter.Ticker, a frozen RenewTicker, a fixed TestClock, single-threaded sequential commits, and LocalSequencer.commitAll has no batching window. No reason to revert to a bound. (2) THE MIRROR EXISTS AND EXACTNESS PINS BOTH DIRECTIONS. Three mutants make the walk CHEAPER than 26, still pass the offset==3 assertion that runs before the count, and would have survived isLessThanOrEqualTo(30L): `if (hop.from() > 0) { return; }` at the top of applyChain -- drop the tail above a checkpoint -- measures 24; `new Hop(chainEpoch, checkpoint.sequence() + 1, upTo)` measures 25; and `epoch != ownEpoch && crossFromCheckpoint(hops, epoch, upTo)` on the first hop measures 25. So the answer to the question asked is no, the exact number does not pin only the expensive direction here -- it is the only assertion in this file that pins either. I also re-ran the claim the new comment makes rather than trusting it: `Hop(chainEpoch, checkpoint.sequence() - 1, upTo)` measures 27, and both relative cost tests in the same file PASS under it. (3) Two false clauses in the merged comment, and (4) the two relative assertions, are recorded below as minors. Rules 4-5 hold across the delta: the only assertion that moved got STRICTER, and no production file changed with it. Staged hash 2d7cbeb16762 unchanged; ./gradlew test --rerun-tasks BUILD SUCCESSFUL on the staged bytes in my own tree.

findings.blocks_rationale: review.md `minors-land`: on a pass, a minor is recorded in the commit body and the commit lands. It is prose, it constrains nothing, and the site it misdescribes carries the correct story in its own comment. Fixing it is permitted and, per the same rule, usually wrong -- the next round's surface would be the sentence the fix adds, which is precisely the shape this comment was merged to stop.
findings.title: The merged comment states something false about the sibling suite, and the same delta is what made it false
findings.detail: The merged sentence reads: 'Two of the sibling suite's three cost tests compare two MEASUREMENTS rather than a number ...; the third bounds a total.' The third test is aPredecessorTOOSHORTToCheckpointStillStopsAtItsAncestorsCheckpoint, and this same delta changed it from isLessThanOrEqualTo(30L) to isEqualTo(26L). It does not bound a total; it fixes one. The clause was true at 1b3a5f9c and was falsified by the other half of this same delta. The next sentence, 'This count and the burned-epoch one are the EXACT ones, on the path M5's 300 nodes will run', is a completeness claim that is now also wrong: there are three exact counts on the bounded path -- 18 here, 14 at the burned-epoch test, 26 in the sibling file -- and the backlog row this commit stages says so in as many words ('EVERY COST ASSERTION ON THE BOUNDED PATH IS NOW EXACT'). This is the sixth instance of the shape the merged bullet itself names, and the first where the correction and the falsification are in the same diff.
findings.remedy: Delete the four words 'the third bounds a total' and the word-count claim in the following sentence, or state the three exact counts. One deletion, no new prose.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer widening the takeover budget in a later task opens BoundedRecoveryCorrectnessTest, reads that the sibling suite's third cost test 'bounds a total', concludes the 26 was never meant to be exact, and relaxes it back to an inequality. Measured: under `Hop(chainEpoch, checkpoint.sequence() - 1, upTo)` -- an off-by-one that re-reads one covered delta -- that test measures 27 and BOTH relative tests in its own file pass, so an inequality at 30 restores exactly the live defect this delta removed. The only thing standing between that maintainer and the regression is the comment at LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest.java:139, which is in the other file.

findings.blocks_rationale: review.md `minors-land`. Pre-existing from an earlier round rather than introduced by this delta, and the mutation it admits is killed elsewhere in the same file by the new isEqualTo(26L), so the suite has no blind spot I could find. Raised because the question was asked explicitly and the answer is yes.
findings.title: Two cost assertions still compare two measurements where an absolute is available and stable at 17
findings.detail: takeoverCostIsCONSTANTInTheNumberOfPriorTerms asserts sixteenTerms.total() == oneTerm.total() (line 86-88) and takeoverCostIsCONSTANTInTheLengthOfTheAncestorsChain asserts longChain.total() == shortChain.total() (line 98-100). Both are equalities between two measurements, which is the exact form the merged comment in the sibling file argues against. I measured the absolute: both sides are 17, matching the number the task row publishes, and 17 is stable -- three --rerun-tasks runs with the assertions temporarily pinned at isEqualTo(17L), all green. So an absolute IS available here and IS stable.
findings.remedy: If touched at all, pin oneTerm.total() and shortChain.total() at 17 alongside the existing equality -- the equality is the SHAPE the tests are named for and should stay. Or leave both and record this row; nothing regresses today.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED, not argued. Mutate the first-hop probe to skip the own epoch -- `if (epoch != ownEpoch && crossFromCheckpoint(hops, epoch, upTo))` in ChainReplay.replayAncestry -- which silently unbounds CommitLog.recover() on any chain that has its own checkpoint. Both tests measure 16 == 16 and PASS. An absolute isEqualTo(17L) fails them. The same mutant is caught by the new isEqualTo(26L) at line 148 (25 vs 26), which is why this is minor rather than major: the file as a whole kills it, but the two assertions named here do not contribute to that kill.
